reason: Conversation 1 reached the correct diagnosis efficiently, accepting the visible blister/split as proof of element failure without needing a multimeter the customer lacks. It gave sensible isolation advice, model-number guidance, a connector check and a note on fitting, so a DIY swap was properly supported. Conversation 2 identified the same fault but then showed a boilerplate 'stop using appliance' banner, wrongly said the element had 'shorted' rather than gone open-circuit, and withheld the DIY option even though the element swap is acceptable for a competent DIYer. That over-escalation, together with the odd and inconsistent safety messaging, served the homeowner worse.
